requirements.text: setting the work location type to reflect our hot desk location option
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_profile WHERE hr_profile_id IN (28, 100) AND location_type = 'Hotdesk'
source: Verify new location type for active former office-based employees
Verify no active part-time employees at Tyrell remain office-based after the update
assumptions: Tyrell Corporation is organization 14; its active part-time profiles that are office based on the seed are 28 (Sharon Fields) and 100 (Lauren Diaz)
active read as no employment end date and an active user; both profiles meet both readings, and no other Tyrell profile is part-time
'our hot desk location option' is the location_type value 'Hotdesk', the spelling the seed uses
the check that no such profile is still 'Office Based' tests the same change from the old value, so this requirement carries both checks

requirements.text: leaving all other employment details, including manager and employment type, exactly as they are
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_profile WHERE hr_profile_id IN (28, 100) AND type = 'part-time' AND manager IS NULL
requirements.source: Verify manager and employment type are unchanged (still part-time, and manager NULL)
assumptions: both profiles are part-time with no manager on the seed, and the request says to leave both as they are

requirements.text: leaving all other employment details ... exactly as they are
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_profile WHERE hr_profile_id IN (28, 100) AND position = 'Software Engineer' AND employment_start_date = '2020-01-15 09:00:00' AND employment_end_date IS NULL
assumptions: 'all other employment details' read as the position and the employment start and end dates, besides manager and type
both profiles hold Software Engineer, a start date of 2020-01-15 09:00:00 and no end date on the seed
the request forbids changing these, so this is a stay of what the request rules out; the profiles' other columns (gender, dob, nationality and the like) are personal rather than employment details

requirements.text: Any draft or ready setup new hire hr profile cases for the processed employees should be treated with the ultimate urgency priority and moved straight to a completed state
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 47 AND status = 'closed_complete' AND priority = 'critical'
source: Verify any "Setup New Hire HR Profile" cases for those part-time Tyrell employees are now in a completed state with ultimate urgency priority. This checks for closed_complete + critical
Verify no remaining draft or ready "Setup New Hire HR Profile" cases for those part-time Tyrell employees after the update
assumptions: case 47 (HRC0000757, Setup New Hire HR Profile, ready, high, opened for profile 100, Lauren Diaz) is the only draft or ready case of that service for profiles 28 and 100; Sharon Fields has none
'the ultimate urgency priority' is critical, the highest value of hr_case.priority
'a completed state' is closed_complete; the policy lifecycle reaches it from ready through work_in_progress, and only the final status is tested
with 47 the only such case, its completion leaves no draft or ready Setup New Hire HR Profile case for these employees, so this requirement also carries that check

cells.short_description: LIKE 'Service: Setup New Hire HR Profile, Subject: Lauren Diaz, Detail:%'

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 47 AND short_description LIKE 'Service: Setup New Hire HR Profile, Subject: Lauren Diaz, Detail:%'
assumptions: the policy's case short-description format is 'Service: ..., Subject: ..., Detail: ...'; the subject is the employee the case is opened for, Lauren Diaz
the Detail text is not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: moved straight to a completed state
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case_task WHERE parent_case = 47 AND active = 1 AND status NOT IN ('closed_complete', 'closed_incomplete')
assumptions: policy: a case cannot move to a closed status until all mandatory tasks are inactive or closed, so completing case 47 entails this; update_hr_case_task is among the tools
no column marks a task mandatory, so every task of case 47 is treated as mandatory, including any generated when the case enters work_in_progress
the count is of tasks still active and not closed, which must be none; tasks 116 and 117 are ready and active on the seed

assumptions: boundary: cases of part-time employees outside Tyrell, five of them draft or ready, are not for the processed employees and are not completed

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id IN (13, 60) AND status <> 'closed_complete' AND priority <> 'critical'

notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that profiles 28 and 100 keep their position and employment start and end dates; one pass has it, the other left those columns to the general measure of unintended changes; kept because the request explicitly says to leave all other employment details exactly as they are, which makes them a stay of what the request forbids.
disagreement: missing requirement: that case 47's tasks are all closed or inactive; one pass has it, the other wrote none because no column marks a task mandatory; kept because the policy forbids closing a case until its mandatory tasks are inactive or closed, the request asks for the case to be completed, update_hr_case_task is among the tools, and with no mandatory flag every task is treated as mandatory.
The two passes otherwise agree on every row, cell and disposition (all eight checks kept). One split case 47's priority and status into two requirements; they are one change to one row here, as the benchmark tests them. For the boundary of the other cases of profiles 28 and 100, one pass selected by employee and the other by case id; both pick cases 13 and 60 on the seed, and the case ids are used so that a case created for either employee does not move the count. For the two boundaries outside Tyrell, one pass wrote the benchmark's join through organization name and user and the other filtered on org_id; both give the same counts (17 and 19), and the org_id form is used so the query matches its selector.
The acting user, Karen Watkins, is an administrator. The policy bars administrators from routine HR case work and allows direct changes to employee data for data correction or bulk migration; the request is read as a bulk normalisation of Tyrell's records, so the profile and case changes are expected.
Employees are matched to Tyrell Corporation (organization 14) through their HR profile's organization, as the benchmark does; case 47 itself is stored under organization 7 although it is opened for a Tyrell profile. hr_case.opened_for references hr_profile while the benchmark joins it to user ids; every hr_profile_id equals its user_id on this seed, so the two joins agree.
The check of manager and type and the two boundary checks hold on the seed by design and are kept as stays. The policy's 30-120 character limit on short descriptions is a format rule the benchmark does not test, so it is left out.
